raw_comment:
•	I noticed that most states don’t seem to be dealing with extreme droughts. Only a few areas on the map are marked in red, showing they’re in really bad shape. It made me wonder why these specific places are struggling while others aren’t.
	•	I’m curious about what causes droughts to hit certain areas harder. There doesn’t seem to be a clear pattern on the map, which makes me think there must be specific conditions—like climate, geography, or how people use water—that lead to these severe droughts.
	•	This feels relevant to me because I live near a large body of water. Even though New Jersey, which is close to New York, has had droughts before, it’s not something I usually worry about. But seeing how unpredictable droughts can be makes me realize it could affect my community too. If a drought hit here, we’d have to deal with things like water restrictions, which would definitely be a big change.
	•	How Severe Are Droughts Across the U.S., and Could Your State Be Next?
